% Round 74 (referee round 6, item 7): first-order radiometric chain at the element observable, generated by
% reproduce/radiometric_budget_observable.py (functions of reproduce/radiometric_budget.py); numbers in outputs/radiometric_budget_observable.json.
\begin{table*}[t]
\caption{First-order radiometric chain of the baseline MIR spectrograph for one $0.5$-km sample at a $20$-km tangent, with the sourced uncooled VO$_x$ microbolometer ($D^{*}=10^{9}$~cm\,Hz$^{1/2}$\,W$^{-1}$, $17$-$\mu$m pitch, $12$-ms time constant). The solar irradiance is the $5772$-K disk model anchored to the ASTM~E490 value at $10~\mu$m; the element signal is spread over $2\times112$ pixels (two spectral pixels per $0.1$-$\mu$m element, the solar diameter across the slit); detector noise is $\sqrt{A_\text{tot}}/D^{*}$ over those pixels with a noise bandwidth $1/(2t)$; the exo-atmospheric reference is the mean of $100$ samples above $80$~km. The attenuation at $8.80~\mu$m is the element observable $-\ln\langle T\rangle$ of Appendix~\ref{app:tracegas_element} with the sulfate background included; at $11.40$ and $20.40~\mu$m it is the element average of the mean optical depth, an upper bound on the attenuation. The random terms are given separately as fractional errors of the ratio at the attenuated sample: shot noise grows as $e^{y/2}$ with the element optical depth $y$, the additive detector noise as $e^{y}$, and the systematic transmission floor of $5\times10^{-4}$ is a per-sample, per-element term whose covariance is not established. ``SNR'' is the per-sample transmission SNR of the ratio, $T/\sigma_T$; the systematics cap of $2000$ is applied afterwards. The two dwell values bracket the $1$--$3$~km\,s$^{-1}$ descent of the tangent point.}
\label{tab:radiometric_budget}
